title: daisybio/domainsplit pipeline parameters
description: A nextflow pipeline to split domain-domain interaction data into train, validation, and test while reducing data leakage and bias.

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Unused samplesheet placeholder; this pipeline reads inputs from the url_* parameters instead.
input.help_text: Kept for nf-core template compatibility. Source databases are configured via the url_* parameters in nextflow.config.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

source_database_options.title: Source databases
source_database_options.description: Public source databases (URLs and local file paths) used to assemble the domainsplit database.

url_3did.description: URL of the 3did SQL dump archive.

url_pfam_regions.description: URL or path of Pfam-A.regions.tsv.gz, FETCH_DOMAIN_META's instance source: every Pfam region of every reference-proteome protein, with no redundancy reduction. Deliberately not Pfam-A.fasta, which is 90% non-redundant and drops the human member of well-conserved families.

pfam_regions.description: Local Pfam-A.regions.tsv.gz, skipping the ~4.7 GB transfer.

cache_dir.description: One cache root for every download this pipeline caches: ppi-splitting's Pfam/UniProt files under pfam-<release>/ and the per-organism STRING links under string/. Must be an absolute path on a filesystem every compute node shares. A convenience only: a cold run produces identical output.
cache_dir.help_text: ppi-splitting's own param name for this is interpro_cache, which is kept as a legacy alias; passing either works and cache_dir wins.

uniprot_dat_urls.description: Comma-separated UniProt flat files (URL or path) that ARE the run's protein universe, Swiss-Prot first. Leave unset: it is derived from instance_tier. PARSE_SWISSPROT reads them once and emits the GO-term TSV, the accession-to-Pfam TSV, the protein FASTA and the STRING-id map; FETCH_DOMAIN_META reads the same list as its protein universe, because Pfam-A.regions carries coordinates only and the domain sequence, taxon and review flag come from here.
uniprot_dat_urls.help_text: Set explicitly only to pin a release or point at local copies. Swiss-Prot must come first: an accession promoted from TrEMBL to Swiss-Prot between releases exists in both files and both parsers take the first writer, so the reviewed record has to be the one they see. Derived defaults: human_reviewed -> uniprot_sprot_human.dat.gz (114 MB); all_species_reviewed -> uniprot_sprot.dat.gz (667 MB); human_any_review_status -> uniprot_sprot_human.dat.gz + uniprot_trembl_human.dat.gz.

swissprot_taxon_ids.description: Comma-separated NCBI taxon ids kept while parsing the UniProt flat files; an empty string keeps every species. Leave unset: it is derived from instance_tier ('9606' for the human_* tiers, empty for the all_species_* ones).
swissprot_taxon_ids.help_text: Set explicitly only to narrow further, e.g. '9606,10090' together with --instance_tier all_species_reviewed for a human+mouse run. Note that `--swissprot_taxon_ids ""` on the command line is parsed by Nextflow as a bare boolean flag and rejected; use an all_species_* tier, or a -params-file.

url_negatome.description: URL or path of the Negatome non-interaction TSV.

url_string.description: One explicit STRING links file (URL or path). Leave unset: FETCH_STRING_LINKS then derives the taxon list from the STRING ids of the proteins in the database and downloads STRING's per-organism links file for each, so every species the universe admits is enriched. Setting it pins that one file and skips the fetch, which is what -profile test does to stay offline.

string_release.description: STRING release used to build the per-organism download URL: https://stringdb-downloads.org/download/protein.links.v<rel>/<taxid>.protein.links.v<rel>.txt.gz

string_min_proteins_per_taxon.description: Skip a taxon contributing fewer than this many proteins, so one stray protein does not cost a 50 MB STRING download. 1 fetches for every taxon present.

url_pfam2go.description: URL of the Pfam2GO mapping file.

negative_ppi_parquet.description: Required path to a Y2H/MS PPI parquet (columns: gene_name_bait, gene_name_prey, n_tested, ...). BUILD_CANDIDATE_NETWORK maps bait/prey genes to UniProt then Pfam (via UniProt REST API) and emits every tested-but-non-interacting Pfam pair, restricted to families appearing in a 3did DDI, as the pool ppi-splitting's `ilp_candidates` sampler draws from.

negative_ppi_min_n_tested.description: Minimum value of the `n_tested` column required to keep a PPI row when building the candidate network from negative_ppi_parquet.

negative_ppi_gene_mapping.description: Optional `gene_pfam_mapping.json` from an earlier BUILD_CANDIDATE_NETWORK run. Supplied, the gene → UniProt → Pfam lookup is read from it instead of the UniProt REST API — the only way the pipeline runs fully offline. Genes the file does not cover count as unmapped.

seed.description: Master random seed. Passed to ppi-splitting and used by every sampling step on this side, so a run is reproducible from this one number.

ddi_examples_target.description: Concrete instance pairs representing one DDI. Passed through to ppi-splitting and used by BUILD_EXTERNAL_TEST, so the external test set is sized like the splits.

ddi_examples_pool_factor.description: Instances drawn per Pfam family before instance pairs are formed, as a multiple of ddi_examples_target. Bounds the work, not the result.

instance_tier.description: The run's protein universe, and the only one of these four params you have to set: uniprot_dat_urls, swissprot_taxon_ids and ppi-splitting's instance_tiers are all derived from it. Families left with no eligible instance keep none and their DDIs are dropped by PRUNE_UNREPRESENTED_DDIS.
instance_tier.help_text: human_reviewed (~20k entries, default) is human Swiss-Prot. all_species_reviewed (~573k) adds non-human Swiss-Prot. human_any_review_status (~200k) adds human TrEMBL. all_species_any_review_status is NOT IMPLEMENTED and fails before any task is submitted -- it needs the 110 GB TrEMBL flat file, which FETCH_DOMAIN_META cannot hold in memory (daisybio/domainsplit#4). Upstream fills strata in the order human_reviewed -> other_reviewed -> human_unreviewed -> other_unreviewed: reviewed outranks human. Lower strata fill freely rather than as a top-up, so widening the universe reshapes the instance pool of families that were never dropped, not only the ones that were. The retired values are 'human_only' (now human_reviewed) and 'any' (now all_species_reviewed -- NOT all_species_any_review_status).
instance_tier.errorMessage: instance_tier must be one of human_reviewed, all_species_reviewed, human_any_review_status, all_species_any_review_status (unimplemented). The retired values map as: human_only -> human_reviewed, any -> all_species_reviewed.

ddi_mode.description: Route the imported ppi-splitting pipeline through DATA_PREP_DDI, so interaction files hold Pfam family accessions and domain instances are split instead of whole protein chains. Always true for this pipeline.

split_train_fraction.description: Fraction of positive DDIs in the train split, for the `random` and `minimal_leakage` strategies. The `external_test` strategy has no internal test set and uses 1 - split_val_fraction instead.

split_val_fraction.description: Fraction of positive DDIs in the validation split, for every splitting strategy.

split_test_fraction.description: Fraction of positive DDIs in the test splits, for the `random` and `minimal_leakage` strategies. The `external_test` strategy runs with 0 and takes its test set from BUILD_EXTERNAL_TEST.

ppi_splitting_multi_negset.description: Ask ppi-splitting for both ILP negative sets per split — plain `ilp` plus `ilp_candidates`, the same sampler restricted to the candidate network — which turns 3 method directories into 5 and 11 split databases into 18. On by default: the comma-separated `negative_sampling_method` fan-out it needs is in the pinned submodule. The candidate network must be dense enough that every split can cover itself from it: survival is quadratic in a split's share, because both families of a pair have to land in the same split. Set false for a `--split_only` debug run, which ppi-splitting refuses unless `negative_sampling_method` is exactly "ilp".

hippie_tsv.description: Required path to a HIPPIE PPI TSV. COLLECT_DDI_DATA adds positive DDIs inferred from PPIs between two single-domain proteins.

hippie_min_score.description: Minimum HIPPIE confidence score (column 5) required to keep a PPI row when inferring single-domain positive DDIs.

ppidm_tsv.description: Required path to a PPIDM predictions TSV (columns: domain_1, domain_2, class). PARSE_PPIDM emits each DDI twice, under the umbrella source 'PPIDM' and under 'PPIDM_<Class>'; both merge onto one database row.

ppidm_classes.description: Comma-separated PPIDM confidence classes to include.

domain_embedding_options.title: Domain embedding options
domain_embedding_options.description: Which models embed the cut domain sequences, and how that inference is sharded.
domain_embedding_options.help_text: One pooled vector per domain instance per model, published as `<outdir>/embeddings/<model>_domain_embeddings.h5` keyed `{domain_id}/{instance_id}`. Nothing is written into the database: per-residue protein embeddings are retired, because protein context correlates with the interaction partner and slicing a protein embedding smuggles protein identity into a split that was partitioned on families.

embedding_models_domainbench.description: Comma-separated domain-embedding models to run (`esm3`, `esmc`, `prott5`). One GPU task per (model, shard). Set empty to produce no embeddings at all.

embedding_shards.description: Number of FASTA shards the domain sequences are split into. Each (model, shard) pair runs as one GPU task; concurrency is capped by maxForks in conf/modules.config.

embedding_max_len.description: Maximum domain sequence length fed to a model. Longer sequences are skipped (quadratic-attention long tail; would otherwise OOM or stall a chunk).

embedding_batch_size_esm3.description: Initial batch size for esm3 domain inference. Halved in-process on torch.OutOfMemoryError and retried.

embedding_batch_size_esmc.description: Initial batch size for esmc domain inference. Halved in-process on torch.OutOfMemoryError and retried.

embedding_batch_size_prott5.description: Initial batch size for prott5 domain inference. Halved in-process on torch.OutOfMemoryError and retried.

embedding_prott5_model.description: HuggingFace id of the ProtT5 encoder. Ungated, so it needs no HF_TOKEN — unlike ESM3 / ESMC.

embedding_require_gpu.description: Abort an embedding chunk task when no GPU is visible instead of falling back to CPU. CPU inference loads a 1.4B model per task and OOM-kills concurrent tasks rather than finishing slowly, so the failure is worth surfacing immediately. Set false only to deliberately accept CPU inference on a tiny input.

embedding_hf_cache_dir.description: Shared HF_HOME directory for the embedding chunk tasks (e.g. an NFS path). Avoids parallel chunks each re-downloading the gated ESM3 / ESMC weights. Set empty to use the per-task local cache.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
